lines.text: Dad, there's wine in the stew! Am I allowed to eat it?
lines.speaker: pip

lines.text: Sure! When you cook it, all the alcohol burns off.
lines.speaker: leo

lines.text: All of it? Hmm. Let's draw it.
lines.speaker: maya

lines.text: Alcohol boils at about 173 degrees Fahrenheit. Water boils at 212.
lines.speaker: leo

lines.text: But in the pot they're all mixed up, so they leave together, a little in every puff of steam.
lines.speaker: leo

lines.text: What about setting it on fire? A flambé looks dramatic, but about three quarters of the alcohol stays in the pan.
lines.speaker: leo

lines.text: Simmer for fifteen minutes, and almost half is still there. After one hour, about a quarter.
lines.speaker: leo

lines.text: Even after two and a half hours, about five percent stays in the stew.
lines.speaker: leo

lines.text: So a quick splash at the end keeps most of the alcohol. A long, slow stew keeps only a little.
lines.speaker: maya

lines.text: Cooking for kids, or for someone who doesn't drink? Use broth, juice, or alcohol-free wine instead.
lines.speaker: maya

lines.text: Actually, wait. So cooking never takes out all the alcohol. The longer it simmers, the less is left.
lines.speaker: theo

lines.text: Then does it matter which wine you cook with?
lines.speaker: pip
